The most appropriate ground is **Speech or Debate Clause immunity** (U.S. Const. art. I, §6, cl. 1), which absolutely protects a member's floor speech as legislative activity, so the suit fails whatever the falsity or fault allegations. The team note's two options are weaker: federal sovereign immunity doesn't reach a suit against a senator in a personal capacity, and the actual-malice standard only matters if the speech is not immune.

CONFIDENCE: 80
